Binghamton University, State University of New York
Bachelor of Mathematical Sciences in Statistics; Minor in Digital and Data Studies
Expected Graduation: June 2027 · GPA: 3.8/4.0



Biostatistics; artificial intelligence for health; bioinformatics; statistical learning; cancer biomarker discovery; mental health evaluation; mixed-methods research; reproducible data science; interactive data visualization.




June 2026–Present Quantitative Paid Intern, First-Year Research Immersion Program — Binghamton University
Faculty Mentors: Dr. Megan Fegley and Dr. Caitlin Light

Contribute 10 hrs/week of quantitative expertise to FRI program evaluation by developing R Shiny dashboards, integrating dissemination records, and designing Qualtrics surveys.
Develop Google Apps Script automation workflows to process survey responses into spreadsheets and organize publication and presentation records.
Visualize student outcomes and dissemination metrics in interactive R Shiny dashboards to support program evaluation and reporting.



June 2026–Present Mental Health Workshop Quantitative Paid Summer Intern — Binghamton University
Faculty Mentor: Dr. Shane McCarty

Contributed 60 hrs of quantitative expertise to a mental health workshop by designing evaluation surveys, developing quantitative methods, and building individualized wellness profiles.
Designed Qualtrics surveys to evaluate mental health literacy, well-being, nonviolent communication, and workshop effectiveness.
Developed an interactive wellness webpage using Claude and Observable JS to visualize survey results and generate individualized wellness profiles.






November 2025–Present Transcriptomic Biomarker Discovery and Validation in Chemo-Immunotherapy — Independent Study, NSF REU Research Stipend, Binghamton University
Faculty Mentors: Dr. Nancy Guo

Contribute 10 hrs/week to chemo-immunotherapy biomarker discovery by reproducing RNA-seq and scRNA-seq preprocessing, clustering TCR expansion with K-means, and analyzing treatment-response signatures.
Transform and validate single-cell RNA-seq data through quality control, normalization, gene filtering, and highly variable gene selection.
Perform differential expression analysis, cross-study comparisons, and Gene Set Enrichment Analysis to identify and validate treatment-response biomarkers and biological pathways (manuscript in preparation).



August 2025–Present Machine Learning for Health Information Avoidance — Independent Study, Binghamton University
Faculty Mentors: Dr. Heather Orom (University at Buffalo), Dr. Shane McCarty and Dr.Kargin Vladislav

Predict health information avoidance in colorectal cancer using logistic regression, multivariate adaptive regression splines (MARS), and random forest classifiers in R with tidymodels and caret.
Evaluate and compare model performance using cross-validation and predictive metrics, documenting results in a reproducible Quarto and LaTeX report (manuscript under review).



August 2025–APR 2026 A Mixed-Methods Analysis of Promotion and Prevention Mindsets — Undergraduate Research, Binghamton University
Faculty Mentor: Dr. Shane McCarty

Contributed quantitative analyses to a mixed-methods study integrating statistical modeling with team-conducted qualitative coding on community health and safety perceptions.
Applied logistic regression modeling in R to investigate whether promotion and prevention mindsets predict health and safety-related goal preferences.
Served as first author on a poster abstract accepted for the 2026 APHA Annual Meeting and co-authored a 2025 Society for Community Research & Action presentation.



August 2023–December 2024 First-Year Research Immersion (FRI): Community & Global Public Health — Undergraduate Research, Binghamton University
Faculty Mentor: Dr. Shane McCarty

Collaborated with a 7-person team to research the impact of Endometriosis on women’s mental health, culminating in two poster presentations to peers and faculty at FRI conferences in December 2023 and 2024.
Conducted quantitative data analysis using SPSS for 6+ hrs/week to examine vaccine hesitancy among pregnant women.
Designed and distributed a comprehensive campus-wide survey using Qualtrics, collecting and analyzing responses.



June 2025–Present Examining Zero-Sum Beliefs and Political Affiliation — Undergraduate Research, Binghamton University
Faculty Mentor: Dr. Shane McCarty

Examine political party affiliation and zero-sum beliefs as predictors of voter choice in the 2024 U.S. election.
Analyze group differences using ANOVA/Kruskal-Wallis tests, logistic regression, and machine learning classification in R; synthesize findings into a scientific report (manuscript in preparation).

January 2025–May 2025 R Programming Peer Mentor — First-Year Research Immersion Program, Binghamton University
Faculty Mentor: Dr. Shane McCarty

Mentored students in foundational R programming, team-based research, and Quarto reporting across public health projects.
Collaborated with the instructor and other research assistants to support research teams’ Quarto research reports.






January 2026–Present Histopathology Thyroid Cancer Detection Using YOLO — Group Project, Binghamton University | Group project

Develop a YOLO26-based deep-learning workflow for thyroid cancer, abnormal, and normal histopathology tissue detection, including model training, evaluation, and error analysis.
Evaluate model performance through Type I (false positive) and Type II (false negative) error analysis and interpret confusion matrices for class imbalance and dataset representativeness.
Visualize and document model performance and limitations for potential pre-screening applications (manuscript in preparation).



September 2025–December 2025 Deep Reinforcement Learning in Board Games — Group Project, Binghamton University | Group project

Implemented deep reinforcement-learning agents in PyTorch to play Tic-Tac-Toe and Connect Four through self-play.
Designed neural networks mapping board states to action values and visualized training performance using Matplotlib.






September 2026–Present Graphic Designer — Binghamton AI Society, Binghamton University

Design the club logo and promotional materials, including event posters, workshop graphics, and outreach visuals.

section: Predicting Health Information Avoidance in Colorectal Cancer
text:
Predicting Health Information Avoidance in Colorectal Cancer
Independent Study, Binghamton University
Faculty Mentors: Dr. Heather Orom (University at Buffalo), Dr. Shane McCarty, and Dr. Kargin Vladislav
August 2025–Present

Predict health information avoidance in colorectal cancer using logistic regression, multivariate adaptive regression splines (MARS), and random forest classifiers in R with tidymodels and caret.
Examine political affiliation as a predictor of cancer-information avoidance, vaccine skepticism, and climate-change skepticism.
Fit regression models adjusted for demographic covariates and estimate covariate-adjusted marginal means.
Evaluate and compare model performance using cross-validation and predictive metrics, documenting results in a reproducible Quarto and LaTeX report (Manuscript in preparation)

About me
My work combines statistical modeling, machine learning, survey design, mixed-methods analysis, and interactive data visualization to address questions in public health and healthcare. I enjoy building reproducible workflows and accessible research tools using R, Python, Quarto, R Shiny, Observable JS, Qualtrics, and GitHub.
